nodes.natural_language: We restate the theorem as the target claim to prove.
nodes.statement: Find all real x satisfying cos²x + cos²2x + cos²3x = 1

nodes.natural_language: Apply the power-reduction identity ϵθ=(1+cos2θ)/2 to each term.
The original equation is equivalent to cos2x+cos4x+cos6x=-1.
nodes.statement: cos^{2}x+cos^{2}2x+cos^{2}3x=1 \Leftrightarrow cos2x+cos4x+cos6x=-1

nodes.natural_language: Solve the factored sine equation for 	heta and back-substitute to obtain all real x.
nodes.statement: All real solutions are x = k\pi/2 or x = \pm\pi/3 + 2k\pi/3 for integer k

nodes.natural_language: Substitute 	heta=2x and apply the Dirichlet kernel sum formula to the left-hand side.
nodes.statement: cos	heta + cos2	heta + cos3	heta = [sin(3	heta/2)·cos(2	heta)]/sin(	heta/2) with 	heta=2x

nodes.natural_language: Clear the denominator and rearrange the resulting trigonometric equation into a product of sines that factors cleanly.
nodes.statement: sin(	heta/2)·(2cos2	heta+1) + sin(3	heta/2) = 0 after algebraic rearrangement

nodes.natural_language: Factor the sum after setting 	heta=2x: cos	heta + cos2	heta + cos3	heta = cos2	heta(2cos	heta + 1).
nodes.statement: cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = cos4x(2cos2x + 1) = -1

nodes.natural_language: Rearrange into a product equation and solve the resulting cases cos4x = 0 or 2cos2x + 1 = -1/cos4x, but better convert to polynomial in cosines or sines.
nodes.statement: cos4x(2cos2x + 1) + 1 = 0 leads after substitution to sin factors

nodes.natural_language: The original equation is equivalent to sin^{2}x+sin^{2}2x+sin^{2}3x=2.
nodes.statement: cos^{2}x+cos^{2}2x+cos^{2}3x=1 \Leftrightarrow sin^{2}x+sin^{2}2x+sin^{2}3x=2

nodes.natural_language: Set u=2x and rewrite the equation cos2u(2cos u +1)+1=0 as a polynomial in cos u after double-angle expansion.
nodes.statement: cos2u(2cos u +1)+1=0 expands to 2cos^{3}u + cos2u +1=0 which factors as (2cos u +1)(cos2u +1) - cos u =0 after trig identities

nodes.natural_language: Convert the factored form into a product of sines via Weierstrass or auxiliary angle substitution and solve the resulting sin(k u)=0 cases.
nodes.statement: After substitution the equation reduces to sin(u/2)·sin(3u/2)·(2cos u +1)=0 or equivalent clean product

nodes.natural_language: Using sum-to-product on cos2x+cos6x yields the equivalent equation cos4x(2cos2x+1)=-1.
nodes.statement: cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = cos4x(2cos2x + 1) = -1

nodes.natural_language: The identity sin^{2}	heta=(1-cos2	heta)/2 applied to sin^{2}x+sin^{2}2x+sin^{2}3x=2 recovers cos2x+cos4x+cos6x=-1.
nodes.statement: sin^{2}x + sin^{2}2x + sin^{2}3x = 2 \Leftrightarrow cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = -1

nodes.natural_language: Both approaches reduce the problem to solving the same trigonometric equation.
nodes.statement: cos^{2}x + cos^{2}2x + cos^{2}3x =1 \Leftrightarrow cos2x + cos4x + cos6x =-1

nodes.natural_language: Factor LHS via sum-to-product identities to obtain a product equation ready for case analysis.
nodes.statement: cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = cos4x(2cos2x +1) =-1

nodes.natural_language: Multiply the equation cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = -1 by 2 sin x and convert products to sums.
nodes.statement: sin(3x) + sin(5x) + sin(7x) - sin(x) = 0

nodes.natural_language: Apply sum-to-product identities repeatedly to obtain a product of sines.
nodes.statement: sin(x)·sin(2x)·(2cos(3x) + 1) = 0

nodes.natural_language: Solve the three cases sin x = 0, sin 2x = 0 and 2cos 3x + 1 = 0 separately.
nodes.statement: x = k\pi/2 or x = m\pi/2 or x = \pm\pi/3 + 2k\pi/3

nodes.natural_language: Letting t=cos2x and using cos4x=2t^{2}-1 produces the equivalent equation (2t^{2}-1)(2t+1)=-1.
Expanding and simplifying yields 2t(2t^{2}+t-1)=0, so cos2x=0 or 2cos^{2}2x+cos2x-1=0.
Solve the cubic equation 2t(2t^{2}+t-1)=0 in t=cos2x to obtain the three roots t=0, t=1/2, t=-1.
nodes.statement: cos2x=0 or cos2x=1/2 or cos2x=-1

nodes.natural_language: Back-substitute each cosine root and solve the resulting elementary trigonometric equations for real x.
nodes.statement: cos2x=0 \Rightarrow x=k\pi/2; cos2x=1/2 \Rightarrow x=\pm\pi/3+2k\pi/3; cos2x=-1 \Rightarrow x=\pi/2+k\pi

nodes.natural_language: Both given equivalences reduce the original problem to solving the auxiliary equation cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = -1.
nodes.statement: cos^{2}x + cos^{2}2x + cos^{2}3x = 1 \Leftrightarrow cos2x + cos4x + cos6x = -1 (via either cosine or sine power-reduction)
